note: Promotion to the tracked schema (v0.91.0, prompt 3 tranche two). Each theme in this pack names exactly one row at one grade band, not five rows across the ladder, so "unbanded": true fills each row's empty description with its own complete sentence directly — no per-band suffix, since the row already names its own grade. track/code are not filled by this promotion (see tools/normalize_blocks.py apply_promotions): this pack's natural sub-groupings do not form the 50-block tracked shape. Theme text and grouping are copied verbatim from data/blocks.csv; nothing else is touched.

themes.description: Name every language spoken in a classroom and one person who speaks each.
Collect five local words with the person who taught them to you.
Record a sentence spoken by a family member and write it down together.
Pronounce every name in a classroom correctly, checked by their owners.
Retell a family story accurately to the person who told it to you.
Find five objects with names in two languages spoken at a school.
Identify three sounds one language has that another language does not.
Propose a spelling for an unwritten local word and test it on three readers.
Obtain and record consent before publishing a collected language item.
Produce a clean recording that a reviewer accepts on the first pass.
Transcribe two minutes of speech and mark every uncertain word.
Build a ten-term glossary with a stated source for each entry.
Read to a younger learner who can then retell the passage back.

themes.theme: The word for the thing at work (LA)
themes.description: Collect twenty trade terms from a working practitioner and verify them.
Explain why a machine translation is not an author, using a real example.
Draft a family signal reviewed and corrected by two native speakers.
Rewrite a message in three registers and have each judged appropriate.
Document three untranslatable terms and the strategy chosen for each.
Review a peer's draft to the author's stated satisfaction.
Prepare a draft to seal-ready state and pass a reviewer's checklist.
Deposit a collection with metadata a stranger could use in ten years.

themes.theme: A language is not a costume (LA)
themes.description: Identify and correct a decorative misuse of language in real published material.
Present a real orthography debate and the decision the community made.
Build and document a small consented corpus with provenance for every item.
Test a language tool and publish where and how it fails.
Teach a lesson that a non-speaker can pass a check on.

themes.theme: Materials for a family, not a linguist (LA)
themes.description: Produce family materials that three families use without asking a question.
Draft a consent and rights agreement a community lawyer approves.
Complete an elder collaboration the elder describes as respectful.
Assemble a complete promotion file for a language against the published criteria.
Convene a circle that produces reviewed material for a full block.
Document a real divergence and produce a route that respects both sides.
Train a reviewer who independently seals a draft you did not touch.
Produce a two-year sustainability plan a community board adopts.
Publish a Tier 0 pack in a language that prints correctly unaided.
Write the refusal memo for a real shortcut and defend it to a panel.
Present a complete promotion to a panel that includes the language's own reviewers.
Repeat an instruction for a classmate so they can act on it.

themes.theme: Say it the way they said it (IN)
themes.description: Carry three messages between two people with no change of meaning.
Complete a five-turn exchange without interrupting either speaker.
Stay out of a scripted disagreement while carrying it accurately.

themes.theme: Ask when you do not know (IN)
themes.description: Ask for a repeat three times in one exercise without hesitation.
Explain the privacy rule of interpreting in your own words to a younger child.
Render five two-sentence turns with no omissions.
Carry ten numbers and names with zero errors under observation.
Use notes to carry a forty-second turn accurately.
Carry a full exchange in first person without slipping into third.
Carry three difficult sentences without softening any of them.
Set up a three-person interpreted conversation correctly.
Manage pace in a fast exchange without losing content.
Handle five unknown terms by the published strategy, not by guessing.
Refuse three scripted invitations to advise while staying helpful.
Explain the harm of child interpreting and name the alternative in your area.
Prepare and use a domain glossary in a live simulation.
Interpret a full simulated conference and pass the observer's rubric.
Translate a three-hundred-word document and pass a second reader's check.
Sight-translate a one-page form with no material error.
Flag two real cultural mismatches without a single group generalisation.
Complete a consent process a supervisor accepts.
Interpret a simulated clinical encounter under a qualified observer.
Interpret a simulated hearing with a verbatim record check.
Complete a remote assignment, including a handled technical failure.
Self-correct three seeded errors within the same turn.
Produce a staffing plan for a four-hour assignment and justify it.
Map the real certification route for a language and produce a plan.
Translate a Tier 0 sheet and test it with three families.
Decline three scripted assignments correctly and offer the right referral.
Design a language-access service a real administrator calls workable.
Train an interpreter who passes an independent observation.
Deliver a maintained glossary that two departments adopt.
Publish a policy on machine assistance a review panel accepts.
Complete a crisis simulation with accuracy verified against the record.
Negotiate a scripted contract to terms a practicing interpreter approves.
Present a portfolio to a panel that includes a certified interpreter.
Name the maker and the reason behind three things seen today.
Take two photographs of one scene that tell different stories.
Sort ten items into three piles and defend the unsure pile.
Obtain consent from three people before photographing them.
Recount a real event that a witness confirms is accurate.

themes.theme: Listening to a recording of yourself (MC)
themes.description: Record, listen to, and improve a thirty-second telling.
Trace three claims to a source or mark them as untraceable.
Conduct an interview the subject says was comfortable and accurate.
Produce a recording a listener can follow with no visual at all.
Edit an interview to half length and get the speaker's approval.
Caption a piece and have a deaf or hard-of-hearing reviewer approve it.
Publish a correction to your own work within a day of finding the error.
Publish an accurate local piece with two named sources.
Audit a published local story for missing voices and go get one.
Verify or debunk three circulating items and publish the method used.
Complete an archived oral history with signed consent and metadata.
Cover three public meetings and publish accurate accounts of each.
Publish a data-led piece a statistician calls fairly stated.
Produce a photo set the subjects approve for publication.
Produce a public notice a stranger acts on correctly at first reading.
Add a documented item to a real local archive.
Identify manipulation in three real examples and state the check used.
Publish a four-part series on a local subject with named sources.
Obtain and report from a real records response.
Resolve five scripted ethics cases and defend each to an editor.
Produce a labelled synthetic piece and a matching detection write-up.
Deliver a five-minute documentary the subjects approve.
Deliver a piece through three channels and measure which one reached whom.
Complete a risk assessment an experienced journalist signs off.
Publish a piece produced with an interpreter and credit them by name.
Run a publishing operation for a term with a published corrections log.
Edit five pieces to the writers' stated satisfaction.
Publish a corrections policy adopted by a real outlet or school publication.
Produce a funding plan with written independence guarantees.
Deliver a public explanation an affected audience calls clear and honest.
Deliver a documented archive a successor uses without instruction.
Present a full portfolio to a panel that includes a working editor.
